subtopics.title: The Five Number Summary and the Box-and-Whisker

questions.question: For the marks 44, 48, 50, 52, 53, 55, 56, 58, 60, 84, the median is:
The lower quartile of this dataset is found by:
options: Taking the median of the bottom five values, giving 50
Dividing the minimum by four
Averaging the two smallest values, giving 46
Taking a quarter of the maximum, giving 21

questions.question: The interquartile range of the marks is:
The range is a fragile measure of spread because:
options: It requires the data to be sorted first
It uses squared units
It ignores the maximum
It depends entirely on the two most extreme values

questions.question: For the data 4, 6, 7, 9, 14, the deviations from the mean of 8 sum to:
options: 0 — deviations from the mean always cancel exactly
14 — the largest value
58 — the sum of squares
8 — the mean itself

questions.question: The variance of 4, 6, 7, 9, 14 is:
The standard deviation is the square root of the variance because:
options: Square rooting removes negative signs
The variance is in squared units, and rooting returns to the units of the data
The calculator cannot display variance
It makes the answer smaller and easier to write

questions.question: The five steps for standard deviation, in order, are:
options: Sort, quartiles, median, box, whiskers
Square, sum, mean, deviations, root
Mean, deviations, square them, average the squares, square root
Root, average, square, deviations, mean

questions.question: Skewness is named after:
options: The hump, where most data sits
The side with the higher frequency
The position of the mode
The tail — the side that stretches further

questions.question: For the test marks, mean 56 and median 54 signal:
options: Positive skew — the mean is dragged toward the long right tail
Negative skew — the data leans left
Perfect symmetry
An arithmetic error, since mean and median must be equal

questions.question: The mean chases the tail because:
options: The mean only counts the number of values
The mean is always the largest measure of centre
The mean shares out the total, so distant values drag it their way
The tail contains the most values

questions.question: On a box plot, positive skew typically shows as:
options: A median bar exactly in the middle of the box
A longer right whisker, with the median bar shifted left in the box
Two whiskers of equal length
A box wider than both whiskers combined

questions.question: The outlier fences are placed at:
options: The minimum and maximum
One standard deviation either side of the mean
Q1 and Q3 themselves
Q1 − 1,5 × IQR and Q3 + 1,5 × IQR

questions.question: With Q1 = 50, Q3 = 58 and IQR = 8, the upper fence is:
Removing the outlier 84 changes the standard deviation from about 10,4 to about:
options: 12,6 — it increases
4,7 — it collapses to less than half
10,4 — it is unaffected
0 — the data becomes constant

questions.question: When outliers are present, the recommended measures to report are:
options: Mean and standard deviation, because they use every value
Range and mean, because they are quickest
Median and interquartile range, because they are robust against extremes
Mode and range, because they need no calculation

questions.question: In the road-of-houses picture, the box of a box plot represents:
options: The two most extreme houses
The house exactly at the mean
The whole road from start to end
The middle half of the houses — the ordinary neighbourhood

questions.question: The whiskers of the box plot are:
options: The roads out from the box to the first and last houses
The distances from the mean to each quartile
Error bars showing measurement uncertainty
The two houses closest to the median

questions.question: Measuring the road end to end corresponds to the range, and its weakness is that:
options: It cannot be calculated without a calculator
It uses squared units
Moving one extreme house changes the whole answer
It ignores the maximum value

questions.question: A compact box with one very long whisker tells you:
options: The data was recorded incorrectly
Most values sit close together, with a stretch out to a distant extreme
The median equals the mean
The data is perfectly symmetric

questions.question: Averaging the signed distances from the mean always gives:
options: The variance
The interquartile range
The standard deviation
Zero — values below the mean exactly cancel values above

questions.question: Squaring the deviations does two jobs:
options: Halves the data and doubles the mean
Makes everything positive and punishes big strays more than small ones
Sorts the data and removes duplicates
Converts the data to percentages and rounds it

questions.question: In the shooter's picture, the standard deviation of 3,41 means:
options: The shooter's best match was 3,41 goals
The team wins 3,41 matches on average
A typical match sits about three and a half goals away from the average of 8
The shooter scores 3,41 goals per match

questions.question: A rival shooter also averages 8 goals but with standard deviation 1,2. She is:
options: More consistent — her matches stray far less from the average
A weaker shooter overall
Certain to score 8 in the final
More likely to score 14 in a match

questions.question: The fences stand at one and a half neighbourhood-widths beyond:
options: The mean on each side
Each end of the box — beyond Q1 and Q3
The minimum and maximum
The median bar

questions.question: The conclusion about 84 should be written as:
options: 84 looks too big, so it is probably an outlier
84 is the maximum, so it is an outlier
84 is an outlier because the teacher said so
84 is greater than the upper fence of 70, therefore 84 is an outlier

questions.question: The standard deviation reacts so strongly to the mansion because:
options: It is calculated from the maximum value only
It counts the number of houses twice
Squaring makes distant values shout — their deviations dominate the sum
It always equals half the range

questions.question: Fences are built from quartiles rather than the mean because:
options: Quartiles cannot be moved by the very extremes being tested
Quartiles are always whole numbers
The mean is too difficult to calculate
The rule predates the invention of the mean
